items.question: Is IWE Code a code editor?
items.answer: Yes. IWE Code provides text editing, syntax highlighting, undo, and autosave. Git revisions and comparison views remain read-only.

items.question: Do I need to move my projects?
items.answer: No. Add existing local folders to your workspace. IWE Code keeps their folder structure.

items.question: Can I use it without a GitHub account?
items.answer: Yes. Browse local projects and Git history without signing in. Private pipelines and job actions require a connected provider account.

items.question: Which languages can I use?
items.answer: The application and this website support English, Russian, and Spanish.

items.question: How are my changes saved?
items.answer: Text files autosave after a short typing pause. If saving fails, the editor keeps your draft and shows an error.

items.question: Can I turn off modules?
items.answer: Yes. Git, pipelines, deployment, and terminal modules start enabled. You can disable each module in settings.

modules.label: Modules
modules.title: Build your own module.
modules.description: Extend IWE Code with external modules. Package a program, describe its panel in JSON, and install it from a file.
modules.intro: An external module is a separate program that IWE Code runs and talks to over a simple JSON protocol. Write it in any language, ship binaries for your platforms, and install the package without recompiling the application.
concept: Your module runs as its own process. IWE Code starts it when you enable the module and stops it when you disable or remove the module.
The host and the module exchange one JSON document per line through the standard input and output of the process.
The module describes its panel with a declarative widget tree. IWE Code renders the panel with its own native components.
The module localizes its own panel text. The host reports the interface language at startup.
modules.manifestIntro: Every package contains a manifest.json file that describes the module.

manifestFields.description: Unique identifier in lower-case kebab style, for example hello-module.
Localized texts. English is required; Russian and Spanish are optional.
Semantic version of the module. Updates must increase it.
Protocol version. The current version is 1.
Minimum application version the module supports.
Executable file name per platform target, for example macos-aarch64.
Declared access: filesystem-read, filesystem-write, network, process.
Workspace zone for the panel: header, top, left, right, or bottom.

modules.packageIntro: A package is a gzipped tar archive with the .iwe-module extension.
modules.protocolIntro: Every message is a single JSON line. Unknown messages are ignored, so modules can stay simple.
modules.hostTitle: From IWE Code to the module

hostMessages.name: initialize
hostMessages.description: Sent once at startup. Reports the protocol version, application version, interface language, and the installation path.

hostMessages.name: event
hostMessages.description: Reports a widget interaction: a click, a toggle, or a text change.

modules.moduleTitle: From the module to IWE Code

moduleMessages.name: panel
moduleMessages.description: Replaces the panel content with a new widget tree.

moduleMessages.name: notify
moduleMessages.description: Shows a short message with an info, warning, or error level.

modules.widgetsIntro: A panel is a tree of simple nodes. Each node has a type and its own fields.

widgets.name: column, row
widgets.description: Stack child nodes vertically or horizontally with an optional spacing.

widgets.name: text
widgets.description: Show text with a body, heading, caption, muted, or danger style.

widgets.name: button
widgets.description: A labeled button that reports a click. Styles: primary, secondary, danger.

widgets.name: text-input
widgets.description: A single-line input that reports value changes.

widgets.name: checkbox, toggle
widgets.description: Boolean controls that report their new state.

widgets.name: separator, scroll, spacer
widgets.description: Layout helpers for dividing, scrolling, and filling space.

modules.permissionsIntro: The manifest declares the access a module needs. IWE Code shows this list before installation and asks for confirmation. Modules run with your user rights; IWE Code does not sandbox them. Install modules you trust.
modules.buildIntro: Build the reference module, assemble the package folder, and compress it. The example is a complete Rust module you can copy.
modules.installIntro: Open Settings → Modules in IWE Code, choose Install from file…, review the requested access, and confirm. Updates install the same way with a higher version number.
modules.exampleIntro: The repository contains a working example under examples/hello-module.
